cases.expected: The returned Set<ValidationMessage> is exactly the set returned by the overloaded validate(executionContext, node, node, atRoot()) call.
cases.description: When both ExecutionContext and JsonNode are non‑null, BaseJsonValidator.validate should delegate to the four‑argument overload and return its result.
If the ExecutionContext argument is null, the method should throw a NullPointerException before delegating.
If the JsonNode argument is null, the method should throw a NullPointerException before delegating.

cases.expected: The atRoot() method is invoked exactly once and its result is passed as the fourth argument to the overloaded validate method.
cases.description: Ensures that BaseJsonValidator.validate uses the path returned by atRoot() as the instance location for validation.

cases.expected: A non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing messages produced by the concrete subclass’s four‑argument validate implementation.
cases.description: When a concrete subclass (e.g., MinimumValidator) overrides the four‑argument validate, the single‑argument validate should return the messages generated by that subclass.

cases.expected: The overloaded validate(executionContext, node, originalNode, atRoot()) receives the same instance for the third argument (originalNode) as the node supplied to the single‑argument validate method.
cases.description: Verifies that BaseJsonValidator.validate forwards the original JsonNode unchanged, i.e., the reference identity of the third parameter equals the original node.

cases.expected: RuntimeException with message "forced error" is thrown
cases.description: A concrete subclass of BaseJsonValidator overrides the four‑argument validate method to throw a RuntimeException. The test asserts that the single‑argument validate method does not catch the exception and propagates it unchanged.
The overridden four‑argument validate returns Collections.emptySet(). The test confirms that BaseJsonValidator.validate returns an empty set rather than null or a non‑empty collection.

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing exactly one message whose text includes "TEXT"
cases.description: A subclass implementation records the runtime class name of the node argument and returns a ValidationMessage containing that name. Supplying a TextNode ensures the validator works for primitive nodes and that the correct node instance is passed through.

cases.expected: Two consecutive calls to validate return equal Set<ValidationMessage> instances (equals() true) and the overloaded validate is invoked exactly twice.
cases.description: Ensures that repeated invocations with the same arguments delegate each time and produce identical results, confirming no hidden state is cached inside BaseJsonValidator.validate.

A concrete subclass of BaseJsonValidator overrides atRoot() to return null and the four‑argument validate method dereferences the supplied path (e.g., calling path.toString()). When BaseJsonValidator.validate forwards the null path, the overridden method throws a NullPointerException which must propagate unchanged.

A concrete subclass of BaseJsonValidator overrides atRoot() to throw an IllegalStateException. The BaseJsonValidator.validate method should not catch this exception; it must propagate the IllegalStateException to the caller.
